prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: World University Rankings 2024: Top Seven (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "University" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Country" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Score" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Overall rank" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "University" · longest unbreakable word 109px · one-line width 277px
  col 2: header "Country" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 111px
  col 3: header "Score › Teaching" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 4: header "Score › Research" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 67px
  col 5: header "Score › Citations" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 65px
  col 6: header "Score › Industry" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 60px
  col 7: header "Overall rank" · longest unbreakable word 51px · one-line width 86px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare the top seven universities by overall rank and four component scores, with country as context.","reading":"Readers identify a university, follow its row across to compare scores and rank, and scan down individual score columns to compare institutions. On a phone, horizontal scrolling separates some of those comparisons from the university names.","groups":["University and Country identify each institution and provide context.","Teaching, Research, Citations and Industry are parallel measures under the shared Score header and should have comparable widths.","Overall rank summarizes position and should remain easy to distinguish from the component scores."],"keep_intact":["University names as recognizable word sequences, without splitting individual words where possible.","Country names and individual numeric scores.","Rank numbers and the individual words in column headers."],"may_wrap":["University names can wrap at spaces; longer names can use multiple lines.","United Kingdom and United States can wrap between words.","Overall rank can wrap between its two words.","The two-tier score header already creates height that can accommodate wrapping in University, Country and Overall rank."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[130,82,86,88,86,81,72],"idea":"Preserve whole words and values at a total width of 625px, accepting horizontal scrolling and several lines for long university names."},{"name":"B","widths":[180,100,86,88,86,81,72],"idea":"Give university names and countries more room for easier row identification at a total width of 693px, trading a longer scroll for less wrapping."},{"name":"C","widths":[100,70,55,55,55,55,60],"idea":"Use a compact 450px table to reduce scrolling while retaining room for numeric scores, accepting splits in long university names and score headers."}]}
